annotations.title: Break-even ROAS for Facebook, Instagram and Google ads

description: Works out the ROAS (ad revenue ÷ ad spend, as Meta or Google reports it) at which Facebook, Instagram or Google ads pay for themselves, when the ad sends buyers to a Shopify store, an Etsy listing or an Amazon listing, with that platform's own fees on the order. Break-even ROAS = order ÷ what one ad order keeps after the platform's fees, product, label, packaging and refunds; that amount is also the most an ad can cost per order. It fits a seller who asks what ROAS they need, why ads with a ROAS of 3 still lose money, or whether to pause Meta or Google ads. Takes the item price, product cost and label; optionally the platform (shopify default), shipping charged, packaging ($1 typical, flagged), the refund share, and the platform's own field (Shopify plan, Amazon category and fulfillment fee). The monthly ad spend with the reported ROAS or ad revenue adds the monthly gain or loss and the fix; all orders a month check the ad platform's count against the seller's own orders. Returns the order line by line, what an ad order keeps, the margin, the break-even ROAS, and with spend the monthly gain or loss. Says that Meta and Google count purchases with their own attribution windows, so their ROAS can differ from the store's own orders. US dollars; dated rates with sources. Free, no sign-in. Takes numbers only; nothing is stored.

adRevenue.description: Optional: the purchase value the ad platform reports for the last 30 days, US dollars. Send with adSpendMonthly; ROAS = adRevenue ÷ adSpendMonthly.

adSpendMonthly.description: Optional: ad spend in the last 30 days on Meta (Facebook, Instagram) or Google, US dollars. With roas or adRevenue it gives the monthly gain or loss.

category.description: Amazon only: the referral category, or not-sure. Left out: Everything Else (15%), flagged.

fulfillmentFee.description: Amazon only: the FBA fee per unit (Fee Preview) when Amazon ships it, US dollars. Left out: 0 (the seller ships), flagged.

itemPrice.description: The average order before shipping, US dollars: what the buyer pays for the item (one item an order).

labelCost.description: The shipping label per order, US dollars (0 if Amazon ships it).

ordersPerMonth.description: Optional: all the orders the store or shop had in the last 30 days, from every source, a whole number. Send with adSpendMonthly: checks the ad platform's count against your own orders.

packaging.description: Packaging per order in US dollars, or mailer (about $1), box (about $3) or not-sure. Left out: $1, a weakly sourced typical figure, flagged as a default.

platform.description: Where the ad sends buyers: shopify (the store), etsy (an Etsy listing) or amazon (an Amazon listing). Left out: shopify, flagged.

productCost.description: Product or materials cost per order, US dollars (Amazon: landed cost).

refundShare.description: Optional: the share of orders refunded in full, a fraction from 0 to 0.9 (0.05 is 5%). A refunded order is counted as: the item comes back and can be sold again, the buyer pays the return label, and the seller loses the label, packaging and the fees the platform doesn't return. Left out: no refunds, flagged.

roas.description: The ROAS the ad platform reports (Meta Ads Manager or Google Ads, last 30 days): ad revenue ÷ ad spend, as a plain number such as 2.5. Google shows ROAS as a percent: 250% is 2.5. Or send adRevenue with adSpendMonthly. Left out: only the break-even is returned.

shippingCharged.description: What the buyer pays for shipping on that order, US dollars (0 if free). Left out: 0, flagged.

shopifyPlan.description: Shopify only: the plan, which sets the Shopify Payments card rate. Left out: basic, flagged.

name: sellerprofit_ads_roas_breakeven

adCostPerOrder.description: Spend ÷ adOrdersCounted (= order ÷ ROAS): what each counted order cost in ads.

adOrdersCounted.description: adSales ÷ order total: the orders the ad platform credits to the ads, a month (not rounded).

adSales.description: ROAS × spend, a month: the sales the ad platform credits to the ads.

allOrdersRoas.description: All orders × order total ÷ spend: the ROAS if every order of the month had come from the ads. Under the break-even, the ads can't pay back whatever the ad platform counts.

isDefault.description: True when the value isn't the seller's own number or tap: a default their own figure would replace.

breakEvenRoas.description: 1 ÷ margin: ads pay back at this ROAS or more (Google's percent is this × 100). Null when each order loses money before the ad.

how.description: The working in words a person can redo, such as "6.5% × $40.00".

onRefund.description: What happens to this fee when the order is refunded in full, in plain words.

additive.description: False when this fix's value is part of another fix's, not on top of it.

estimate.description: True when the fix's dollars rest on an estimated fee (Amazon's, by the size and stock Amazon measures): say "about" and "estimated" when quoting it.

monthly.description: What the fix is worth a month in US dollars, at the seller's numbers, if orders hold; null when no monthly total can be known.

ordersCanFall.description: How far orders could fall (a fraction) before the fix leaves the seller worse off; null when there's no limit or it doesn't apply.

text.description: The fix in plain words, with its condition ("if orders hold").

keptPerAdOrder.description: What one order an ad brought keeps before the ad, on average: (1 − refund share) × keptPerSale − refund share × lostPerRefund. Also the most an ad can cost per order. Negative is a loss.

keptPerSale.description: Order − fees − product − label − packaging, on an order that isn't refunded. Negative is a loss.

link.description: Opens the matching page on sellerprofitdoctor.com. Carries none of the figures sent.

lostPerRefund.description: What one refunded order loses: the fees not returned + label + packaging (the item comes back). Null with no refunds.

monthlyGainOrLoss.description: earnedAfterCosts − spend: negative means the ads cost more than they bring in.

notes.description: What the math counts, assumes and leaves out, in plain words.

ownOrdersCap.description: When the ad platform counts more orders than the store had all month: all orders × keptPerAdOrder − spend, the most the ads can earn a month even if every order came from them. Negative means the ads can't pay back at the seller's own orders. Use it instead of monthlyGainOrLoss then. Null otherwise.

rates.description: Which rules the numbers use, as of when, and where they come from.

asOf.description: The day the platform's fee table was last checked against its sources (YYYY-MM-DD).

estimatesLine.description: Amazon only: which figures are estimates (FBA, storage, returns and the rest depend on the size and stock Amazon measures). Say so when citing them.

recheckBy.description: The day the table is due for its next check.

referralFee.description: The referral fee if each rate applies only to its slice of the price.

referralOtherReading.description: Amazon stepped categories (Beauty, Baby, Grocery, Clothing, Lawn Mowers) above a price line: the fee is read on the whole price, which a public Amazon page doesn't confirm; this is the other reading. Null otherwise.

refundShare.description: The share of counted orders refunded in full (0 when left out).

roas.description: The ROAS used: as typed, or adRevenue ÷ adSpendMonthly.

title: Break-even ROAS for Facebook, Instagram and Google ads
